text: David and the commanders of the army set apart for service the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who were to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals. This was the number of the men who did this work according to their service:
Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied at the king's command.

versions.text: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the king's direction.
versions.explanation: The repetition of "direction ... direction" in one short sentence is clumsy when read aloud. Rendering the second phrase "at the king's command" keeps the sense of עַל־יְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ while improving the rhythm.

text: Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah — six in all — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.

versions.text: Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah — six — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
versions.explanation: Only five names appear although the text says "six," which will puzzle listeners. A footnote is worth adding: "Only five names are listed here; some ancient copies add Shimei (compare v. 17)." The slight rewording "six in all" also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer, according to God's promise to raise up his strength. God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

versions.text: All these were sons of Heman the king's seer, given to him through the words of God to exalt his horn. God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
versions.explanation: "Given to him through the words of God to exalt his horn" is opaque for oral reading, and "horn" is an idiom for power or honor. "According to God's promise to raise up his strength" conveys בְּדִבְרֵי הָאֱלֹהִים לְהָרִים קָרֶן more clearly; a footnote may note that the Hebrew reads literally "to exalt his horn."

text: All of them were under the direction of their father for the music in the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman served under the king's direction.
Their number, together with their kinsmen trained in singing to the LORD — all of them skilled — was two hundred eighty-eight.
They cast lots for their duties, small and great alike, teacher along with pupil.
The first lot fell to Joseph of the family of Asaph; the second to Gedaliah, with his brothers and his sons — twelve;

versions.text: The first lot fell to Asaph, for Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he with his brothers and sons — twelve;
versions.explanation: "To Asaph, for Joseph" is a wooden reproduction of the Hebrew and confusing when heard; identifying Joseph as belonging to Asaph's family is clearer. A footnote may note that the Hebrew does not state a number for the first group, which the pattern implies as twelve.
